headline: Tariff refund flatters swing to profit, guidance moves up
summary_short: Columbia Sportswear posted Q2 FY2026 diluted EPS of $0.52 versus a $0.19 per-share loss a year ago, as revenue rose 1.5% y/y to $614.4M and gross margin expanded 920bp to 58.3%, largely on a one-time $78M IEEPA tariff refund.
summary_long: Revenue grew 1.5% y/y to $614.4M as international strength (EMEA +10%, LatAm/APAC +12%) offset continued US softness from lighter Spring wholesale orders and softer DTC brick-and-mortar traffic. Gross margin expanded 920bp y/y to 58.3%, almost entirely from a ~$78M IEEPA tariff refund (~980bp benefit); SG&A rose on store impairments and new-store costs, partly offset by lower tech spend. Operating income and net income both swung from year-ago losses to $30.9M and $26.6M. Cash plus short-term investments ended at $624.6M with no borrowings; the board approved a $0.30/share quarterly dividend. Columbia raised FY2026 gross margin, operating income, and diluted-EPS guidance (all driven by the tariff refund, not underlying demand) while holding net-sales guidance unchanged and citing incremental H2 macro/geopolitical headwinds.

drivers.explanation: International strength (EMEA, LatAm/APAC) partly offset by lower US net sales, primarily lighter Spring 2026 wholesale orders and declines in DTC brick-and-mortar.
Expansion primarily reflects a ~980bp benefit from recovery of IEEPA tariffs, partially offset by unfavorable DTC channel profitability from increased promotional activity.
Swing to profit driven by the tariff-refund benefit in cost of sales; SG&A rose on higher DTC expenses (store impairments, new stores), partly offset by lower enterprise-technology spend.
Diluted EPS benefited $0.93 from the IEEPA tariff-refund recovery; effective tax rate rose to 26.8% from a year-ago tax benefit of 38.5%.

CEO cites resilient international business offset by US softness and macro headwinds; H2 outlook 'incrementally moderated' on geopolitical/macro headwinds, though full-year guidance ranges (ex-tariff impact) are reaffirmed.
